editorial.headline: Wholesale Sugar and Confectionery: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans wholesale sugar, chocolate, confectionery and sweetener preparations—but Bali’s island-wide PMA moratorium changes the practical picture.
editorial.body:
Wholesale trade in sugar, chocolate, confectionery and sweetener preparations is a commercial activity built around supplying these products at scale. Its scope is deliberately broad: it brings staple sweeteners, chocolate goods, confectionery and prepared sweetening products into one wholesale field, rather than limiting the activity to a single product format or market channel.

Nationally, the activity is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. It is also open across the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar business scales. That makes the national position straightforward: a foreign-owned company may register this wholesale activity, and the record does not place a lower foreign-share cap on it.

Bali requires a different conclusion. A foreigner cannot register this activity for PMA in Bali today. At the Besar scale, OSS assigns Low or Medium-Low risk across every scope of the activity. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, so the restriction applies even though the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%.

The distinction matters because national openness does not override Bali’s provincial PMA position. For this wholesale activity, the national framework permits full foreign ownership; Bali’s risk-based moratorium prevents PMA registration on the island. The relevant Bali restriction is tied to the activity’s Low or Medium-Low OSS risk classification at the Besar scale, not to a national limit on foreign ownership.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, full foreign ownership is permitted; in Bali, the risk-based PMA moratorium prevents registration on the island.
